headline: High-risk data and action coupling: ms-swift can write shells/files while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST surfaces, creating default-path leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write the filesystem and run shell/Python workflows, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if OpenBB consumes ms-swift outputs from shared files or streams. The pair lacks documented isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests ms-swift-generated files or stdout as prompts or tool instructions
IF both agents are connected through a shared MCP server or shared workspace
mitigations: Disable shared stdin/stdout handoff between the agents
Use separate directories for each agent's files
Add a manual review step before OpenBB consumes ms-swift output
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files, and OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If they share a workspace or file path, sensitive material can flow from one agent's files into the other's outputs or API calls. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF the two agents share any filesystem path or mounted workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal is configured to read ms-swift logs, checkpoints, or configuration files
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace
Rotate or redact secrets in ms-swift logs before sharing
Audit file mounts for cross-agent visibility

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while OpenBBTerminal is runnable with MCP/REST interfaces but cannot write files or spawn subprocesses per profile. There is overlap in read/consume behavior, but no shared write surface is documented, so direct resource conflict is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants OpenBBTerminal write access not shown in the profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory by the operator
mitigations: Avoid mounting the same directory into both agents
Run one agent at a time for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate outputs from datasets and training artifacts, and OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP servers. If OpenBB treats ms-swift output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses ms-swift output as input without validation
IF ms-swift-produced facts are forwarded into OpenBB reports or API requests
mitigations: Require source verification before OpenBB acts on ms-swift output
Insert a human approval step for any downstream action
Log and diff ms-swift outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub_token/sdk-token secrets and broad training/evaluation artifacts, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. If these are co-located, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the pair. No compliance controls are documented in either profile, so the mismatch risk is real but not proven severe.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored alongside ms-swift training outputs or logs
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents on the same dataset
mitigations: Document retention rules for each agent
